Customer is evaluating hosted vs Dedicated for a pilot; key concerns: per-tenant quotas, SSO/SCIM, KMS/bring-your-own-key, and latency/cost tradeoffs. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jared Kim (Redwood SE), Sarah Nguyen (Lakemont CTO), Carlos Ruiz (Lead Platform Engineer), Priya Rao (Security Architect)

00:00 - Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. We'll do a 30-40 minute walkthrough of rate limits, quotas, and org/project keys in Redwood — show the Console and then the API, then Q&A. Sound good?
00:12 - Sarah: Yep, thanks Maya. We're particularly interested in per-tenant isolation, burst behavior, and how keys map to orgs/projects. We run on AWS EKS and a mix of serverless for some services.
00:25 - Maya: Great, Jared will drive the demo, I'll chime on pricing and the pilot. Jared?
00:28 - Jared: Thanks. Quick context check — do you already have rate-limiting at the app layer, Carlos?
00:36 - Carlos: Yeah, we do NGINX + sidecar based limits, but it's messy. We want platform-level guarantees for the LLM calls and the ability to scope per-customer quotas. Also HIPAA considerations.
00:48 - Jared: Understood. We'll show org-level and project-level keys, how they enforce quotas and rate limits, and hybrid routing policies (hosted vs dedicated).
01:00 - Jared: (shares screen) This is the Redwood Console. Top left you see org switcher — we map a top-level org with projects underneath. In our demo org I've predefined two projects: prod and pilot. Each project has its own API key, quota, and rate-limit bucket.
01:18 - Sarah: Quick Q — can keys be scoped to a service account or person? We want to rotate keys and attribute usage back to internal teams.
01:26 - Maya: Yes, keys can be user-scoped or service-scoped, and we provide token-level attribution in our cost/latency breakdowns. We also support project-level roles for RBAC.
01:40 - Jared: Here on the project settings you can see 'Request quota' and 'Burst window'. Quota is enforced daily/monthly units and burst window controls short-term TPS.
01:50 - Jared: (typing) I'll show the live policy: prod has 1M tokens/day, 200 TPS bursting to 400 for short periods; pilot is 50k tokens/day. You can apply rate limit overrides per-route too.
02:07 - Carlos: How strict is the enforcement at the edge? If we exceed burst does it queue or return 429s?
02:14 - Jared: We do soft queuing up to a small buffer to avoid immediate 429s, but once the buffer is full policies return 429. For Dedicated you can configure larger buffers and autoscale.
02:26 - Sarah: That buffer sounds good; our critical path can't block for long though. We care about predictable p99 latency.
02:33 - Jared: For p99 we recommend Dedicated or a pinned hosted tier — that avoids noisy neighbor effects. Our routing can also fallback to a cheaper model variant if capacity constrained.
02:46 - Maya: From a commercial perspective, a small Dedicated commit gives you guaranteed GPU pools and predictable latency. Pricing options I'll send after the call.
03:00 - Jared: Switching to API view — calling the Redwood API, you include an Authorization header with the project key. The response includes X-RateLimit-* headers for remaining quota and reset window.
03:12 - Jared: (shows curl) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer proj_key_ABC" https://api.redwood.sh/v1/generate... and you'll see headers like X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset.
03:27 - Carlos: Do we get webhooks or pushes when an org hits quota? We want alerting into our incident system.
03:34 - Jared: Yes, you can enable quota webhooks per org or project; we also integrate with PagerDuty and send events to your configured webhook URL.
03:44 - Priya: On the security side: KMS, BYOK, and audit logs — what's supported for Private and Hosted?
03:51 - Maya: Hosted supports customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS). Private deployments can integrate with HSMs. Audit logs and exportable event streams are available on Dedicated and Private. We'll share the security whitepaper.
04:10 - Sarah: Are logs redacted by default? PHI concerns.
04:15 - Jared: We have configurable PII redaction pipelines and data retention policies. For HIPAA workloads we suggest Private or Dedicated with stricter retention controls.
04:26 - Jared: Back to the Console — you can set org-level default quotas, then override per-project. Here's the project key issuance flow — generate key -> assign roles -> enable usage limits -> optional IP allowlist.
04:40 - Maya: Note: keys are intended for server-to-server use. For client-side we recommend short-lived tokens or a proxy.
04:50 - Sarah: How do you do multi-tenant billing? We need per-customer cost reporting.
04:55 - Jared: Redwood Console has token-level cost breakdowns by project, route, and model. You can download CSVs or call our billing API for programmatic attribution.
05:10 - Jared: Now I'll demo the API rate limiting behavior under burst. I'm going to run a small load test against the pilot project key to show headers and 429 behavior. (starts demo)
05:22 - Jared: 00:05 into the test — responses look normal, headers showing remaining tokens.
05:36 - Jared: 00:45 — now we increased concurrency — see a few 429s, then the buffer clears, then more allowed. The log shows rate limit reasons: "burst_exceeded" and then "quota_exceeded" if sustained.
05:55 - Carlos: Helpful. If we want stricter per-customer limits inside a single project, can we use sub-keys or metadata?
06:03 - Jared: You can issue multiple keys per project or ship a customer_id as X-Customer-Id header and Redwood's routing/aggregation can enforce per-customer throttles via our policy engine.
06:16 - Priya: About SCIM/SSO and RBAC — we need SCIM provisioning for project roles and SAML SSO. Is that GA?
06:24 - Maya: SSO/SAML and SCIM are GA for Enterprise plans; we can enable a trial for you. Roles map to Console permissions and API key issuance rights.
06:36 - Sarah: Great. Anything else around securing the keys at rest? Encryption?
06:40 - Jared: Keys are encrypted at rest with CMKs; for Hosted we support customer-managed CMKs (AWS). Private supports HSMs if needed.
06:50 - Maya: I'll drop the security whitepaper and KMS integration doc in the follow-up.
07:00 - Jared: Next, policy examples — per-route limits for chat endpoints vs embeddings. For embeddings we recommend separate project keys since they have different token characteristics and cost per unit.
07:20 - Carlos: We do embeddings at scale; what's the per-second throughput for embeddings on a shared hosted tier?
07:25 - Jared: On hosted it varies by model; typical throughput for a medium model is ~50-100 embedding requests/sec per shared pool; Dedicated can give predictable multiples based on GPU commit. We'll include model performance numbers in the doc.
07:40 - Sarah: Is it possible to have org-level soft limits for cost control that don't block but alert?
07:45 - Jared: Yes, soft alerts and spend thresholds are configurable — they can trigger webhooks, email, or block depending on the policy you choose.
08:00 - Priya: Any tenant isolation guarantees for data residency? We have EU customers that must stay within eu-west regions.
08:07 - Jared: We support region pinning: you can pin an org to a region and routing will prefer that region. For Private you control the physical location.
08:18 - Maya: Many customers start hosted, then move to Dedicated if latency/SLOs or residency needs become strict.
08:28 - Jared: Demoing the 'Create project' flow — set quotas, enable KMS, toggle dedicated routing. You can also define canary rollouts where requests are routed to a canary model variant for a percentage of traffic.
08:42 - Carlos: For canaries does the quota enforcement aggregate across canary and main?
08:47 - Jared: You can choose to have separate quotas or aggregate them. For safe rollouts we usually isolate quotas.
09:00 - (small crosstalk) Sarah: Sorry, quick procurement note — we need contract terms for Dedicated and SLAs.
09:07 - Maya: We'll attach standard SLA language; we can discuss custom terms with legal if you need.
09:15 - Jared: Now switching to Redwood Optimize briefly — this is our cost/perf toolkit. It recommends batching, quantization, and model variants by workload. You can run evaluations against your prompt sets to detect regressions.
09:30 - Sarah: That eval feature would help. We have a set of 120 prompts for clinical triage.
09:38 - Jared: We can import prompt sets and run evals; the Optimize dashboard will show quality delta and cost implications.
09:46 - Priya: For benchmarking, can we spin up a Dedicated trial or do we benchmark on hosted?
09:52 - Maya: We can provision a short Dedicated pilot for sizing, but often we do initial benchmarks on hosted with pinned model variants and then translate to Dedicated sizing. Jared will propose the test plan.
10:08 - Jared: I'll propose a benchmark plan: 1) Baseline on hosted with pilot project key, 2) Run 30-minute burst test, 3) Repeat on a small Dedicated pool. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, and token costs.
10:26 - Carlos: Sounds good. For the test scripts, we prefer the load generator to be compatible with k6 or Locust.
10:33 - Jared: We have sample k6 scripts; I'll share them.
10:40 - (pause, Jared navigates back to Console)
10:50 - Jared: Show project keys page — you can create keys with expiration, IP allowlist, and restrict to routes. Keys can be rotated and audit events show who created/rotated them.
11:05 - Sarah: Who shows up in audit logs if a key is used? We need to map back to internal user IDs.
11:10 - Jared: If you use service-scoped keys with X-User-Id headers, audit logs will capture that metadata. We also support propagating trace IDs for request correlation.
11:22 - Priya: About data retention and deletion — if a user requests deletion, can we purge their data from caches and logs?
11:30 - Jared: We support data deletion workflows and TTLs on logs; for Hosted we'll run purge jobs, for Dedicated/Private you control retention more directly.
11:40 - Maya: I'll include our data retention and deletion SLA notes in the follow-up.
11:50 - Jared: Now a quick look at per-org quota API: GET /v1/orgs/:org_id/quotas and POST /v1/orgs/:org_id/quotas to adjust. You can programmatically adjust quotas on the fly for burst events.
12:08 - Carlos: Do quota adjustments have an audit trail?
12:12 - Jared: Yes, every policy change is auditable with who/when.
12:18 - Sarah: One more question on model fallbacks — if the primary model is unavailable, do you retry to a smaller model automatically?
12:25 - Jared: We have configured fallback policies. You can choose failover to a compatible quantized variant, or route to a cheaper model; retries and circuit breakers are configurable.
12:36 - Priya: For compliance we'll need a runbook for incidents. Is that part of the Enterprise package?
12:42 - Maya: Enterprise and Dedicated customers get an SLO runbook and a named technical contact for incident response.
12:50 - Maya: Quick pause — any blockers to running a pilot?
12:53 - Sarah: Main blockers: procurement + security review. Security wants KMS/BYOK details and a HIPAA attestation. Procurement will want pricing options.
13:05 - Maya: Understood — we'll send the security pack and standard terms.
13:10 - Jared: Demo wrap-up — I'll demo one last thing: dynamic rate limits via API. You can POST a policy change to increase a project's TPS for a scheduled window.
13:22 - Jared: (shows POST) payload includes policy type, target project, limits, and time window. Useful for scheduled campaigns.
13:34 - Carlos: Can we hook those changes to our internal deployment pipeline?
13:39 - Jared: Yes, the API is fully programmable; you can integrate it into your CICD or deployment scripts.
13:46 - (few seconds of typing)
13:50 - Maya: Okay wrapping up: we'll follow up with pricing, security docs, k6 scripts, and a draft benchmark schedule. Jared will own the benchmark and coordinate with Carlos.
13:59 - Sarah: Thanks, this was super helpful. One small note — can you include sample X-RateLimit headers in the docs?
14:05 - Jared: Absolutely, I'll paste examples and show response payloads with headers.
14:11 - Priya: Thanks. Also please include the process for key rotation and emergency key revocation.
14:16 - Maya: We'll include.
14:20 - (closing)
14:22 - Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by end of week.
14:25 - Sarah: Thanks folks.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hears, e.g., "KV cache" was sometimes transcribed as "KV cash", "canary" as "canary" but may be said quickly. Some technical terms abbreviated.
